# `scripts/gadget_pkdgrav3_compare/halo_potential_profile.py`

Source: [halo_potential_profile.py](../../../../scripts/gadget_pkdgrav3_compare/halo_potential_profile.py)

```text
Stacked gravitational potential around halos: mean and scatter of phi in shells of comoving distance r (Mpc/h)
from the halo centres, for halos in mass bins. Gadget-4 HDF5, pkdgrav3 HDF5 or pkdgrav3 .pkc snapshots, so the
same statistic can be compared between codes. Only the stacks (per mass bin) are accumulated and stored, never
per-halo profiles: memory is independent of the numbers of halos and particles.

usage:
  halo_potential_profile.py <kind> <snapshot> <halos> <out.npz> [options]
    kind      gadget   Gadget-4 HDF5: snapshot_<nnn>.hdf5 or the base of snapshot_<nnn>.<i>.hdf5
              pkd      pkdgrav3 HDF5 (snap.<step>)
              pkc      pkdgrav3 compressed snapshot, prefix snap.<step> (needs the potential: dCompPotStep > 0)
    halos     consistent-trees hlist (out_<snap>.trees) or Rockstar out_<snap>.list
  options:
    --mbins 3e12,1e13,3e13,1e14,1e15  halo mass bin edges (Msun/h; column --mass-col, default mvir)
    --rbins 0.02,50,36                log bins in comoving r (Mpc/h): rmin, rmax, number;
            lin:0,50,0.2              or linear bins: rmin, rmax, width
    --weight particle|volume          particle-weighted stack (default: every (halo, particle) pair), or
                                      volume-weighted: the same stack over the points of a regular grid that
                                      carry the code's potential interpolated from its particles (below)
    --vgrid N                         volume weighting: N^3 grid points (default 2 x particle grid)
    --vknn 16                         volume weighting: local linear fit to the k nearest particles' potentials
    --vcache file.npy                 volume weighting: gridded potential cache (written if absent, reused if present)
    --all-halos                       include subhaloes (default: hosts only, pid = -1)
    --max-halos 20000                 at most this many halos per mass bin (random, seed 0); 0 = all
    --target 16384                    dilution: particles expected inside a level's outer radius (below)
    --jk 3                            jackknife: jk^3 sub-cubes of the box (by halo centre) for the error
    --par p.par                       pkdgrav3 parameter file (dSoft) to remove pkdgrav3's softened self-potential
    --offset X                        subtract X (km/s)^2 from every potential (e.g. offset_median, particles.csv)
    --pkc-subsamples 1,3              .pkc only: read only these subsample percents
    --chunk 1048576                   particles per work unit (HDF5)
    --workers N                       processes (default: all cores)

Potentials are peculiar, physical, (km/s)^2, with the conventions of compare_potential.py:
  Gadget-4 Potential / a; pkdgrav3 Potential * U^2 / a (U = 100 L / sqrt(8 pi/3) km/s), .pkc as stored; with --par
  the pkdgrav3 self-term -(105/64) m / dSoft * U^2 / a is removed.

Algorithm. Particles are read in chunks by parallel processes. Each chunk is paired with the halo centres of each
mass bin through periodic KD-trees (cKDTree.sparse_distance_matrix of a halo group against the particles), and every
(halo, particle) pair adds 1, phi, phi^2 and r to its (jackknife region, mass bin, shell) - a few small arrays.
Radial dilution keeps the work per halo constant out to large radii: shell i is assigned level l_i, the smallest
l >= 0 with nbar 4/3 pi r_out,i^3 / 8^l <= --target (nbar = particles read / L^3), and only the particles of the
nested subsample u < 8^-l are paired at that level, u = hash(particle ID) uniform in [0, 1) and independent of phi.
Because u depends only on the ID (Gadget-4 ID - 1 = pkdgrav3 iOrder), runs from the same ICs use the same particles
at every level, so the dilution noise largely cancels in a code-to-code difference. Each shell uses one
level, so its mean and scatter are unbiased; the number of pairs per halo is ~ target x (number of levels) instead
of nbar 4/3 pi r_max^3. At 2048^3 / 200 Mpc/h, 50 Mpc/h holds 5.6e8 particles; with target 16384 the outer level
uses 1/8^5 of them. Cost ~ n_halo x levels x target x (local overdensity), plus reading the snapshot once.

Volume weighting. The particle-weighted mean is a mass-weighted average over the shell: dense parts (filaments,
neighbouring halos) count more than voids. The volume-weighted mean averages over space instead. phi is put on an
N^3 grid of cell centres by a weighted local linear fit to the k nearest particles' potentials (the code's own
potential, not a grid Poisson solution; phi is smooth on the interparticle scale; a plain inverse-distance average is
biased toward the denser side of the neighbourhood, i.e. too deep near structures), and the grid points are stacked
exactly like particles (same trees, dilution by grid index, jackknife). The interpolation reads all particles into
one KD-tree: fine to 512^3 particles; beyond that it must be done slab by slab (not implemented). delta_hm is then
the deviation of the grid-point count from the shell volume (a check: ~0).

Output (npz), mass bin b, shell i:
  r_edges, r_mid (geometric), r_mean[b,i] (pair-weighted), m_edges, n_halos[b], m_mean[b], level[i], frac[i]
  stack_mean[b,i]   mean phi of all (halo, particle) pairs in the shell (particle-weighted stack)
  stack_std[b,i]    standard deviation of phi over those pairs (scatter of the potential in the shell)
  stack_err[b,i]    jackknife error of stack_mean (leave one of jk^3 sub-cubes of halo centres out)
  delta_hm[b,i], delta_hm_err[b,i]   mean matter overdensity in the shell (halo-matter cross-correlation)
  npair[b,i]        pairs used (diluted); npair_eff = npair / frac
  jk_n, jk_s, jk_s2, jk_nh: the per-region sums (region, b, i) / (region, b), to recombine
```

## Contents

- [`read_halos`](#read_halos) - Read a consistent-trees hlist or Rockstar list into lower-case column arrays.
- [`gadget_files`](#gadget_files) - The HDF5 files of a Gadget-4 snapshot: `path` or `path.<i>.hdf5` in order (exits if none).
- [`source_info`](#source_info) - -&gt; (box, a, n\_total, units dict, files or PkcSnapshot)
- [`pkd_selfpot`](#pkd_selfpot) - pkdgrav3 softened self-potential in (km/s)^2 (0 for Gadget-4 or without --par).
- [`parse_rbins`](#parse_rbins) - 'rmin,rmax,n' (log) or 'lin:rmin,rmax,dr' -&gt; (edges, mids, kind)
- [`local_linear`](#local_linear) - phi at the origin from neighbours at offsets dx (n, k, 3) with values f (n, k): weighted least-squares fit f = a + g . dx (weights 1/d), returns a. A plain inverse-distance average is biased where the neighbours lie on one side (dense side = deeper potential); the linear term removes that to first order. Falls back to the inverse- distance average where the fit is ill-conditioned.
- [`vgrid_block`](#vgrid_block) - phi at grid points [p0, p1) of layer i (flat index within the layer), in a forked worker
- [`build_vgrid`](#build_vgrid) - phi on the ng^3 cell centres from the k nearest particles, local linear fit (float32). The tree and the particles are shared with forked workers; each task fits VG\_ROWS grid points (the fit is serial numpy, so the parallelism has to come from processes).
- [`load_grid`](#load_grid) - grid points of layers i0..i1-1: positions (cell centres), phi from the cache, flat index as ID
- [`uhash`](#uhash) - uniform [0, 1) from integer particle IDs (splitmix64): the same particle gets the same u in every code
- [`init`](#init) - Worker initialiser: store the run settings in the module global `G` and build periodic KD-trees of the halo centres of every mass bin in groups of `HALO_GROUP`.
- [`load_unit`](#load_unit) - Read one work unit of particles (an HDF5 slice or one .pkc file/subsample).
- [`work`](#work) - -&gt; per mass bin an array (4, nreg \* nr): pair count, sum phi, sum phi^2, sum r
- [`jackknife`](#jackknife) - n, s: (nreg, nr) sums; nh: (nreg,) halos per region. -&gt; error of mean phi and of the overdensity estimator f
- [`main`](#main) - Command line (see the module docstring): stacked potential profiles around halos per mass bin.

## read_halos

```python
read_halos(path, mass_col)
```

Read a consistent-trees hlist or Rockstar list into lower-case column arrays.

Adds `pid` = -1 for Rockstar lists (no host flag) and `mass` = the column `mass_col`; exits if that
column is missing.

```python
gadget_files(path)
```

## local_linear

```python
local_linear(dx, f, d, h)
```

phi at the origin from neighbours at offsets dx (n, k, 3) with values f (n, k): weighted least-squares fit
f = a + g . dx (weights 1/d), returns a. A plain inverse-distance average is biased where the neighbours lie on one
side (dense side = deeper potential); the linear term removes that to first order. Falls back to the inverse-
distance average where the fit is ill-conditioned.

## build_vgrid

```python
build_vgrid(uts, L, ng, k, workers)
```

phi on the ng^3 cell centres from the k nearest particles, local linear fit (float32). The tree and the
particles are shared with forked workers; each task fits VG\_ROWS grid points (the fit is serial numpy, so the
parallelism has to come from processes).

## load_unit

```python
load_unit(u)
```

Read one work unit of particles (an HDF5 slice or one .pkc file/subsample).

Returns positions wrapped into [0, L), the peculiar potential in (km/s)^2 minus `G['subtract']` and the
particle IDs.
